Parameters of a fitted model

Source: R/model-inspect.R
mt_parameters.Rd

Returns the estimated parameters of a fit in one long table, for every model type that has interpretable parameters:

Usage

mt_parameters(fit)

Arguments

fit

An mt_fit object.

Value

A data.table with stratum, parameter, index (age label, year or position), value and, for Bayesian fits, lower and upper; for ensembles also component, for fits by groups also group.

Details

  • lee_carter(): a (age pattern), b (age pattern of change), k (period index), and the drift and innovation standard deviation of k; with choose_period = TRUE, k of the years of the chosen fitting period and its first year (first_year); with rotate = TRUE also the ultimate pattern b_ultimate; with family = "nb" also the dispersion nb_dispersion (variance mu + phi mu^2; one per age group with a dispersion by age); with jump_off = "filtered" also the filtered index of the last year k_filtered, its standard error se_k_filtered and the state-space estimates filter_sigma, filter_lambda, filter_drift;

  • li_lee(), product_ratio(): the common factor of each group (B, K, its drift and standard deviation), per stratum the deviations a, b, k and their AR(1) coefficient phi and standard deviation, and the number of stratum factors fitted (ratio_order, stratum "model");

  • coda(): the centre a (geometric mean distribution of life-table deaths), the loadings b, the index k with the order (order_k), coefficients (arima_k) and innovation standard deviation (sd_k) of its ARIMA model, the share of variation explained by the component, the parameters of the open age interval (a_open, b_open) or of the Kannisto model of each year (kannisto_a, kannisto_b); the coherent model gives per group of common_by the common a, B, K (with order_K, arima_K, sd_K) and per stratum a, b, k and the ARIMA model of k. coda_causes(): per group, as coda(), with parts by age and cause (b1, k1, b2, k2, ... with several components); with individual = TRUE also the individual components of each cause (b_<cause>, k_<cause>, order_k_<cause>, ...) and the explained variation of each cause (explained_joint, explained_individual), and with weights the weights of the parts (w_part) and years (w_time);

  • coda_multiway(): the ranks used (rank, indexed age, time, population), the common age patterns b, time indexes k (with order_k, arima_k, sd_k), population markers gamma and core g (index p,q,r), numbered with several components, and the share of variation explained; per stratum the centre a, the parameters of the open age interval or of the Kannisto model of each year;

  • tucker3(): the ranks used (rank, indexed age, period, stratum), the factors of age (A1, A2, ...), period (B1, ...) and stratum (C1, ...), the drifts of the period factors (drift_B1, ..., with ts = "rwd"), the core g (index p,q,r) and the share of the sum of squares explained (explained), all of stratum "common"; per stratum the centre a (with centre = TRUE);

  • rwd(): drift and innovation standard deviation per age (and, with observation_noise = TRUE, the variances of level and noise);

  • apc_bayes(): posterior medians and 90% intervals of the age, period and cohort effects (logit scale, bamp's identification), and the Gelman-Rubin statistics (rhat, values below 1.1 indicate convergence) of the identified quantities;

  • p_splines(), cp_splines(): the smoothing parameters over age (lambda_age) and years (lambda_year), the effective dimension (ed), the criterion (bic or aic) and the dispersion (deviance divided by the number of cells minus the effective dimension); with p_splines(overdispersion = "age") the smooth dispersion by age (dispersion), the bias-corrected mean Pearson statistics by age that it smooths (dispersion_raw), its smoothing parameter (lambda_dispersion) and the dispersion tau of these statistics (dispersion_tau); for cp_splines() also the bounds of the rates of ageing and of change per age (ageing_lower, ageing_upper, change_lower, change_upper).

  • saint(): per trend ("trend <group>") the indexes alpha, beta, kappa, zeta by year, the frailty variance sigma2, the pseudo-log-likelihood loglik, the drift and covariance cov of alpha and beta (or, with ecm, the parameters of the error-correction model: a11, a21, a32, a42, C_D, C_delta, lambda, Omega) and the standard deviations sd_kappa, sd_zeta; per stratum with a spread the spread parameters y1 ... y5 by year and their VAR(1) (ar or A, and Omega);

  • relative_model(): per group ("reference <group>") the reference parameters alpha, beta (by age), kappa (by year), gamma (by year of birth), the drift and sd of kappa, the ARIMA(1,1,0) model of gamma (ar_gamma, drift_gamma, sd_gamma), and the log-likelihood, effective number of parameters, number of cells and BIC of the reference part (loglik, npar, nobs, bic); per group ("subpopulations <group>") the common beta and the same statistics of the subpopulation part; per subpopulation alpha, kappa, the drift and sd of kappa and the correlation cor of its innovations with those of each subpopulation of the group;

  • bohk_rau(): posterior medians and 90% intervals of the curve parameters b1 and b2 by age and of the variance and hyperparameters, the least-squares values theta1, theta2 (exponential core model) and the Gelman-Rubin statistics (rhat);

  • apci(): alpha, beta (by age), kappa (by year), gamma (by year of birth; 0 for the cohorts with four or fewer observations), the mean year ybar, the smoothing parameters (lambda_alpha, lambda_beta), the effective dimension ed and the bic, and the ARIMA models of kappa and gamma (order_kappa, arima_kappa, sd_kappa, order_gamma, arima_gamma, sd_gamma);

  • nordpred_apc(): estimates and 90% Wald intervals of the age, period and cohort effects (cohorts by central year of birth) and of the drift, the projected drift, the number of periods fitted, the choice of the recent trend and the p-values of the goodness of fit and of the test for the recent trend;

  • cae(): the common age effects beta1, beta2, ... of each group (rows labelled common <g> (<strata>)), and per stratum the centring a, the period effects kappa1, kappa2, ..., their drift (drift_kappa1, ...; with index = "coherent" the common drift of the group for order 1 and 0 for the others, whose autoregressive coefficients are phi_kappa2, ...), the standard deviation of their innovations (sd_kappa1, ...) and the correlation of their innovations with those of the same order of every stratum (cor_kappa1, ..., indexed by the other stratum); rows of stratum "model" give the mean squared error of the centred log rates (mse) and the approximate BIC of Kleinow (2015, eq. 5; bic).

Fits of wrapped packages (StMoMo, demography) keep the original fitted object in fit$fits[[i]], where the methods of those packages apply.

Wrappers return the parameters of the model they wrap (recalibrated() adds its factors; coupled() adds those of the template, with column component "base" or "template"). For an ensemble(), the rows of each component carry its name in column component, and rows with parameter = "weight" give the weights; components without interpretable parameters (wrapped packages) contribute their weight only. For stratified() and tuned(by = ), the rows of each group carry its name in column group.

See also

summary.mt_fit(), residuals.mt_fit().

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
p <- mt_parameters(mt_fit(lee_carter(), x))
head(p)
#>    stratum parameter  index     value
#>     <char>    <char> <char>     <num>
#> 1:  female         a     30 -7.530513
#> 2:  female         a     31 -7.438225
#> 3:  female         a     32 -7.453512
#> 4:  female         a     33 -7.353122
#> 5:  female         a     34 -7.325712
#> 6:  female         a     35 -7.275708
